The banner exists and can be right: with a code sign-off naming an OLDER commit in abbreviated form (ea04b8d) demo's card was topped with [data-testid=queue-since], the undo icon and '2 commits since W3 Other Reviewer approved this on 2026-08-23.' plus the filter link, which is the true count. But sign-offs the product itself writes are 40-character shas (signCodeReview -> resolveCommit expands them), and changesSince() compares them with listHistory()'s %h (7 characters) using ===, so they never match. Proved it both ways on the same record: sha '22db7ed191e63bc644e4f9a5ed892a918f9fb232' (demo's actual HEAD, clean tree) produced a banner reading 'the branch has moved past the commit you approved since W3 Other Reviewer approved this on 2026-08-23'; the identical record with sha '22db7ed' produced no banner at all, which is correct.
verdicts.defect: review-queue.vue changesSince(): `const at = commits.findIndex((h) => h.ref === code.sha)`. listHistory() formats commits with %h (abbreviated) while sign-offs store the full object id, so findIndex always returns -1 and every real sign-off gets the 'the branch has moved past the commit you approved' clause - false when it has not moved, and it also makes the 'never a banner about nothing' condition (at===0 && !changes) unreachable, so a signed-off change with a clean tree gets a banner claiming a move that never happened. gateFrom() already has sameCommit() for exactly this comparison; changesSince should use it.

verdicts.evidence: Step 1 is wired to githubIdentity() now - the code calls it on mount and on connect - but it can never answer, so the row shows no handle, no scopes and no expiry. With a token stored, [data-testid=barn-import-account] read: 'A token is stored, so a private repository clones too. Studio could not read the account from it: " + String(e.message).replace(/[' with barn-import-account-login and barn-import-account-meta both absent. That trailing text is a fragment of the pod script's own source leaking through as the error message. Root cause reproduced in the pod: the installed bundle emits the node script with a REAL carriage return and line feed inside a regex character class (the bundle's string literal is '...replace(/[\r\n]+/g, " ")...' with single backslashes, so the value contains the control characters), node dies with 'SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: missing /' and echoes the offending source line, and the caller's /BARN-GH-ERR:(.*)/ then matches that echo instead of a real error. Ran the same one-liner via kubectl exec into barn-base-extension and got exactly that SyntaxError and exactly that echoed line.
verdicts.defect: githubApiAnywhere() in extensions.ts (~line 2925, and githubApi() at ~2857 has the same line) builds a node -e script containing the literal regex /[\r\n]+/g. The TypeScript source doubles the escapes correctly, but the built bundle in dist-pkg/barn-0.5.22 carries them singly, so at runtime the emitted script has real CR/LF inside the character class and node never reaches the fetch. Neither githubIdentity() nor listGithubRepos() can succeed with any token, valid or not. Avoid a regex literal with escapes inside the emitted script (for example replace(/\s+/g, ' ') written without backslash escapes, or String.raw), and check the built artifact rather than only the source.

The Name in Studio field sits in step 3 and is derived from the repository: typing the rancher/dashboard URL filled it with 'dashboard' and the hint read 'Taken from the repository. Change it to call it something else here.' Overwriting it with 'W3 Renamed Thing' stuck (the field stopped following the repository) and the hint became 'It will be called w3-renamed-thing.' Setting it to 'base' - a name that already exists here - showed 'base already exists here.' and disabled Import.

Step 2's field takes a pasted URL directly: entering https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/tree/release-2.9 was accepted, the hint read 'Reads as rancher/dashboard.', the name filled with 'dashboard' and the branch control pre-filled with release-2.9. Its placeholder says so ('owner/name, or paste the repository URL') and its hint offers it as the escape from the listing ('Or name one that is not on the list, or paste its URL.'). Garbage ('not a repo at all') is rejected with 'That has to be owner/name, or a github.com repository URL.'
verdicts.defect: There is no separate 'Not listed? Paste a repository URL instead' link revealing a second field - the one repository field accepts both forms. That is a smaller surface than the design draws rather than a missing capability.

verdicts.evidence: The check is real - it clones the repository into a pod without file contents and reports four distinct outcomes, each of which I drove. rancher/dashboard: green (data-tone=pass) 'This looks like a Rancher extension. Found pkg/aks/package.json, pkg/aks/index.ts, a pkg/ directory and the rancher annotations block. It does not say which Rancher it was built against, so Studio cannot tell you what has moved since. This Rancher is 2.15.' octocat/Hello-World: warn, 'This does not look like a Rancher extension. Did not find package.json, index.ts, a pkg/ directory and the rancher annotations block. You can import it anyway...'. A non-existent repo: unknown, 'Studio could not see w3verify/definitely-not-a-real-repo-xyz on GitHub. It may be private, in which case connect GitHub in step 1...'. A non-existent branch: unknown, and Import disabled. The version comparison is against this Rancher's real version (2.15).
verdicts.defect: For an unreadable repository Import stays enabled - deliberate, since a private repo the anonymous check cannot see may still import with the token - so the only thing the check actually gates is a missing branch.

verdicts.evidence: No repository rows are ever rendered, so there is nothing to carry a visibility icon, a visibility word or a relative updated time. The markup for all three exists and is correct (the row template draws repoIcon() lock/book, the private/public word and updatedAgo(each.updatedAt)), and listGithubRepos() returns private/updatedAt, but the call cannot succeed - see 06-import-connected-account for the reproduced root cause. With a token stored, [data-testid=barn-import-repo-list] count was 0 and the note under step 2 read '" + String(e.message).replace(/[. Name the repository below or paste its URL instead.'
verdicts.defect: Blocked behind the same githubApiAnywhere() regex defect. Once listGithubRepos() answers, this row markup should light up unchanged.

verdicts.evidence: The list is implemented but never appears. With no token, step 2 renders only the text field and says why ('Studio can only list your repositories when a token is stored, because the listing is fetched by the pod that holds it'). With a token stored, [data-testid=barn-import-repo-list] is still absent (count 0) because listGithubRepos() throws - the note under step 2 was the leaked script fragment '" + String(e.message).replace(/[. Name the repository below or paste its URL instead.' Root cause reproduced in the pod; see 06-import-connected-account. So the user must still know and type owner/name, or paste a URL.
verdicts.defect: Same githubApiAnywhere() regex defect. The row markup, the single-selection highlight (import-extension__repo--on plus the check icon, derived from repoPath so typing into the field lights the matching row) and pickRepo() all exist and are unreachable.

verdicts.evidence: The search box is conditional on the list having rows (v-if="repos.length"), and the list never loads, so [data-testid=barn-import-repo-search] does not exist in the DOM in either state. Enumerated every input and select inside [data-testid=barn-import-step-2] with a token stored: exactly ['barn-import-repo'].
verdicts.defect: Same githubApiAnywhere() regex defect as 06-import-repo-pick. The filter itself (visibleRepos, matching on fullName, with an 'N of M match' note) is written and untestable until the listing answers.

verdicts.evidence: The .s-modal root is position:fixed and measures 1440x900 at 0,0 with background rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45). Controls behind it are unreachable: document.elementFromPoint over the centre of the 'New extension' button returns the s-modal element, not the button.
verdicts.defect: The tint is rgba(0,0,0,0.45) where the design specifies rgba(20,20,26,0.42).

verdicts.evidence: Three stacked steps, each with a 22x22 round marker, and the states are driven by whether GitHub is connected rather than drawn. Unconnected: step 1 data-state='active' with a rgb(61,152,211) (#3D98D3) disc and a white '1'; steps 2 and 3 data-state='locked' with rgb(240,241,244) discs and grey digits. With a token stored: step 1 data-state='done', marker rgb(62,140,79) (#3E8C4F) carrying an icon-checkmark and no digit, and steps 2 and 3 both data-state='active' with blue discs and white digits, both open for input.

Deliberately stopped short of the clone: a completed import creates a ConfigMap, a Deployment and a pod in the shared barn namespace that other verifiers are working against, and this wave was told not to. Everything short of it is proved. The footer button is the green primary with an icon-download, [data-testid=barn-import-submit], and its gating is a real reading of the form: disabled with no repository, disabled while the pre-import check is running, disabled on an invalid owner/name, disabled on a name that already exists ('base already exists here.'), disabled on a branch the repository does not have, and enabled with octocat/Hello-World + master + a free name. The emitted source is `github:<owner/name>#<branch>`.

With barn-settings holding no data keys (confirmed by kubectl) I opened the dialog and enumerated every button in it: the header close, the footer Cancel and the footer Import, and nothing matching /author/i (count 0). Step 1's only control is the 'Paste a personal access token' link.
verdicts.defect: Deliberate and said out loud in step 1: 'There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own to send you to.' OAuth needs a client id and a callback this product has no server for. Recorded as not-implemented rather than fail because the design's control is genuinely absent, and the copy explains rather than pretends.

verdicts.evidence: In the unconnected state (step 1 active, no token stored) the footer Cancel is enabled and clicking it closed the dialog. barn-settings still has no data keys afterwards, and the extension list was unchanged.

In the unconnected state, revealed the token field, typed 'ghp_FAKE_never_saved' into it and clicked the header X. The modal closed, nothing was stored (barn-settings data still empty) and no extension was created.

Step 1 is headed 'Step 1. Connect GitHub' and carries the paragraph 'Studio clones the repository from a pod in this cluster, which takes a few seconds and happens without leaving this dialog. A public repository needs nothing at all. A private one needs a token, and you can paste it here without losing what you have typed. There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own to send you to.'
verdicts.defect: Two wordings differ from the design and both are corrections rather than gaps: 'a few seconds' rather than 'about fifteen seconds', and the purpose is stated as cloning rather than 'list your repositories and clone one' - the listing is written but cannot answer (see 06-import-repo-pick).

verdicts.evidence: With no token stored, clicking Import from the Studio list opens the same dialog rather than redirecting: the panel measures exactly 680px, the head reads 'Import an extension from GitHub' and the caption under it is the same one-way clone line, 'The repository is cloned into your workspace. Nothing is pushed back until you publish.' Connecting happens inside step 1 of this dialog, so there is no round trip to a settings screen and nothing typed is lost.

With no token stored, [data-testid=barn-import-submit] has disabled=true and a computed opacity of exactly 0.4. Once step 1 is satisfied the same button enables on a valid repository: after taking the 'carry on without connecting' escape and entering octocat/Hello-World with a free name, disabled became false; connecting a token instead unlocks steps 2 and 3 the same way.
verdicts.defect: Import is gated on steps 2 and 3 being unlocked plus a valid repository, and 'unlocked' can also be reached by the 'carry on without connecting' escape rather than only by connecting GitHub. That is deliberate - a public repository clones with no credential - and the escape says so where the design draws the lock.

verdicts.evidence: Read the computed styles off all three markers in both states. Unconnected: step 1's marker is rgb(61,152,211) (#3D98D3) holding a white '1' with data-state='active'; steps 2 and 3 are rgb(240,241,244) with grey digits (color(srgb 0.582 0.582 0.663)) and grey headings, data-state='locked'. After connecting a token: step 1 turned data-state='done' with a green rgb(62,140,79) disc and a checkmark icon, and steps 2 and 3 both turned blue with white digits.
verdicts.defect: The locked disc measures rgb(240,241,244) where the design specifies #F2F3F5.

verdicts.evidence: Genuinely absent, not disabled. With no token stored I enumerated every input, select and textarea inside [data-testid=barn-import-step-2] and [data-testid=barn-import-step-3]: both returned []. Step 3 renders nothing but its greyed heading; step 2 renders one sentence explaining the lock and offering the escape. Both headings compute to the tertiary grey and both markers are the flat grey disc.
verdicts.defect: Step 2's locked body is not empty: it carries 'Locked until GitHub is connected. A public repository needs no token, so carry on without connecting if the one you want is public.' with a working link. The design draws the locked steps bare.

verdicts.evidence: It is a real disclosure, closed by default. Before clicking, [data-testid=barn-import-token-field] does not exist in the DOM (count 0). Clicking 'Paste a personal access token' ([data-testid=barn-import-token-toggle]) renders the field plus a 'Connect' button inside step 1, and the step stays step 1 rather than becoming a separate screen.
verdicts.defect: The design pairs this with 'Authorise with GitHub' separated by the word 'or' and draws it as a ghost button. Here it is a text link at the end of the step 1 paragraph and there is no 'or', because the token path is the only path (see 06a-import-first-authorise).

verdicts.evidence: The field is labelled 'Personal access token', is type=password (so the value is masked) and computes to a monospace face, font-family '"JetBrains Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace' at 12px. Submitting it connects: pasting a throwaway token and clicking Connect turned step 1 into data-state='done' / 'GitHub connected' and unlocked steps 2 and 3 (data-state='active', fields barn-import-repo, barn-import-branch, barn-import-name now present) without the dialog remounting. The token was removed from the barn-settings Secret afterwards.
verdicts.defect: The design shows the value masked except for the ghp_ prefix; type=password masks it entirely.

verdicts.evidence: Under the field: 'Needs the repo scope only. Create one on GitHub with the scope pre-selected. It is stored in a Secret in this Rancher, not in your browser, because the thing that spends it is a pod - which also means it is shared with everyone using this Rancher's Studio, not held per user.' The link's href is https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=repo&description=Rancher%20Extension%20Studio, so the scopes really are pre-selected. Confirmed the storage claim against the cluster: saving wrote the key gh_token into the Secret barn-settings in namespace barn, which is one shared object, not a per-user one.
verdicts.defect: The design's promise is 'stored per user, never inside the extension'. Half holds - it is not in the extension - and the copy corrects the other half out loud rather than repeating it, which is the right call but is a deviation from the drawn text.
